The test image shows a corn plant that has collapsed/lodged, lying flat on the ground. The stalk appears to have broken. The plant is still somewhat green. Key observations: whole plant collapse, stalk breakage, plant lying on soil.

Candidates: Bacterial_stalk_rot (sudden collapse, vascular strands intact), Physoderma_stalk_rot (breaks at first/second node), Anthracnose_stalk_rot (shiny black rind).

The reference images for Bacterial_stalk_rot show plants that collapse suddenly, often still green, with collapse at the lower nodes. This closely matches the test image showing a young corn plant that has fallen flat on the ground while still green — consistent with the description "plants suddenly collapse and fall over with their vascular strands still intact."
